PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called meeting to order at 5:00 pm.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed session at 5:03 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:04 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items:

Item #1 and #3 were not discussed.  

Item #2 - Councilmember Rebollo was absent from the discussion on this item.  Staff made a presentation, City Council provided direction and no reportable action was taken on this item.    

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called meeting to order at 6:05 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Library Director Bautista led the Pledge of Allegiance. 

INVOCATION Councilmember Rebollo offered the invocation.  

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Proclamation Recognizing March 21 as World Down Syndrome Day

PUBLIC COMMENT John Loussazarian, Director of the Montebello YMCA, spoke about the various programs and activities currently offered by the YMCA for the community.

Jasmine Gonzalez, Irma Vargas, and Sandra Gonzalez addressed the City Council regarding tenant protections in the City of Commerce.

City Attorney Tapia explained that the City Council previously adopted the state rent control ordinance as part of the municipal code, allowing the City to treat rent violations as code violations. He noted that, in the past, the City has issued letters to landlords when rent increases exceeded the allowable limits under the ordinance. City Attorney Tapia added that the City is open to meeting with residents and discussing how these violations could be addressed through the City’s code enforcement process.
Antonia Lupercio spoke about need to reopen all libraries to what they were before the pandemic and asked about the status of the Bandini Library. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo Item #4 was pulled for discussion.  

3.. Approval of Minutes

6.. Funding Request for New Modular Office and Removal of Existing Modulars at Veterans Park  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Director Alaniz provided a brief overview of the staff report.

Councilmember Rebollo apologized for the extended delay in acquiring the modular unit, noting that it has been over three years. She acknowledged the disservice this delay has caused the community and emphasized the importance of placing the modular in a location where it can remain for the duration of the project. Councilmember Rebollo requested a clear plan for the unit’s placement, both during and after the remediation at Veteran’s Park. 
Director Alaniz indicated that two potential locations had been identified: the Zindell property or the library area at Veteran’s Park. A discussion followed regarding the most suitable location for the modular unit.

Councilmember Garcia asked about the future of the parks programs, specifically the lunch programs. Director Alaniz responded that, with access to hot running water, the lunch program could continue to operate out of Veteran’s Park.

Further discussion addressed the ongoing remediation at Veteran’s Park. 
Councilmember Lainez expressed concern that the park has been neglected due to the pending project. He emphasized the need for staff to remain focused on the Veteran’s Park project and to keep the Council informed about any delays or issues that arise.

Director Alaniz also noted that, aside from the current situation at Veteran’s Park, youth sports participation at the park is higher than at other park locations.

4.. YMCA Collaboration - Model United Nations Program

2.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 15A, 15B and 15C

SCHEDULED MATTERS

5.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Jimenez provided an overview for the last two weeks.  



7.. Disabled Blue Curb Parking Request at 4485 Lovett Street This item was continued to a future date. 

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Argumedo reported attending the Aquatics Banquet on February 28. He also participated in the JPA Board Meeting on February 12, where the focus was on expanding membership and increasing the number of cities represented in the area. Discussions included potential bylaw changes to allow additional cities to join. Councilmember Argumedo also attended a recent Sanitation District meeting.

Councilmember Rebollo recognized and celebrated International Women’s Day, congratulating and honoring all women. She expressed appreciation to the library for hosting a jazz and poetry panel on Saturday and thanked the Commerce Casino for providing lunch. Councilmember Rebollo also attended a Soroptimist International event, where she had the opportunity to honor local women. Councilmember Rebollo congratulated Jim Crawford on his re-installation as President of the Commerce Business Council and wished a happy 95th birthday to Francis Chica.

Councilmember Garcia shared that she attended the Arts in Public Places meeting, where there was enthusiasm about introducing more public art, including crosswalk murals and installations on Commerce buildings. Councilmember Garcia expressed excitement about these new creative initiatives and wished everyone a happy Women’s History Month.

Mayor Pro Tem Lainez thanked the Montebello YMCA for its ongoing partnership and reported attending the Aquatics Banquet. Mayor Pro Tem Lainez also participated in the “Read Across America” event at the Veterans Library and attended the Commerce Business Council meeting on March 6, where he congratulated Jim Crawford on becoming a three-time President of the Council. He also extended thanks to Robert Taylor and gave a special shoutout to former Councilmember and Mayor Joe Aguilar, who received an award at the meeting. On March 7, Mayor Pro Tem Lainez also attended the “Unplugged” Senior Director's Showcase.

Mayor Altamirano extended congratulations in honor of International Women’s Day and also shared personal news, announcing the birth of his youngest son’s baby earlier that day. He spoke about his visits to public art districts in Austin and Miami, expressing interest in bringing similar art initiatives to the community. He mentioned that a few artists from the Wynwood area may be invited to share their vision and ideas with the City Council.

Adjourned to closed session at 7:19 pm

ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 8:05 p.m.
